newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 20.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 20.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - McDonald's decision to sue two environmental activists for libel in Britain is being described as a public relations disaster that cost the fast-food company an estimated 10 million pounds ($16.5 million), despite the fact that McDonald's won the record-length court case this week.

PARIS - Havas Advertising's plans for external growth will involve a dilution in parent Havas's stake, Havas Advertising chairman Alain de Pouzilhac tells shareholders. Havas and its advertising unit also say they are planning a link with an "Anglo-Saxon" advertising agency or network.

DUSSELDORF - Germany's largest brewing and drinks concern, Brau und Brunnen, says it's cutting its advertising and marketing budget from 80 million marks to 60 million marks (from $46 million to $35 million) and consolidate its brands.

CHRISTCHURCH - New Zealand brewer Lion Nathan is starting a trial of what it describes as the world's first glowing beer tap handles together with a so-called "intelligent" beer handle that can be programmed to flash changing graphics for short term promotions.

HAMBURG - Wunderman Cato Johnson in Germany emerges as the most successful German agency at the New York Ad Festival, snapping up gold and silver medals in the print and radio advertising sections. WCJ, which is 100- percent owned by Young & Rubicam Inc in New York, has its European headquarters in
Eschborn, Germany.
NEW YORK - Think New Ideas Inc, a communications company, completes its acquisition of the assets of Fathom Advertising from Omnicom Group Inc.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Pay-TV group Premiere has signed a long-term film rights deal with Hollywood studios Fox and Dreamworks under which it receives subscription and pay-per-view rights for all feature films they produce.

SYDNEY - Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, teams up with Bill Gates, America's wealthiest, to form an Internet alliance between Packer's television and publishing empire and Gates's computer software powerhouse. The venture will use Microsoft's online technology and will draw content from Microsoft products, Packer's TV arm Nine Network and magazine business Australian Consolidated Press.
BRUSSELS - The European Union has agreed to guarantee the future of public sector broadcasting by exempting public funding from the provisions of EU competition law.

APELDOORN, Netherlands - Dutch publisher Wegener NV believes it has the right media mix to thrive in an increasingly crowded media market place. Chairman Jan Houwert says Wegener can reach the mass market through its regional newspapers while targeting individual consumers via direct marketing.
LONDON - British lottery operator Camelot Group Plc says it will extend the BBC's contract to broadcast the lottery for 12 months from November.

LOS ANGELES - Times Mirror Co says advertising revenues for its newspaper publishing group for the four weeks ending June 1 rose 6.9 percent from a year earlier, to $129.38 million from $121.04 million.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LUXEMBOURG - The European Commission may consider banning new self-cooling drinks cans after European Union environment ministers urge a probe into possible global-warming effects of the cans' refrigerant gas.
BUDAPEST - Volkswagen AG widened its lead in the booming car market in Central and Eastern Europe in April, accelerating ahead of rivals Fiat SPA and Daewoo Group, according to a Reuters survey.
LONDON - Supermarket group Safeway Plc is planning to develop its joint venture with Irish company Fitzwilton Plc into a "powerful all-Ireland business", a spokesman says.

TOKYO - Japanese carmakers are expected to scale back production this year. Honda Motor Co Ltd, hit by sluggish car sales at home, says it will cut domestic output for July. Japan's top five carmakers, except for Mazda Motor Corp, suffered a drop in domestic car sales in May.

LONDON - British drinks giant Guinness Plc says it is watching LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton "with interest" amid speculation that the French luxury goods group will further increase its stake in Grand Metropolitan.
FOSTER CITY, California - Sony Corp's Sony Computer Entertainment America says it expects sales of its Playstation video game player to reach six million units in 1998.
BUDAPEST - The Hungarian unit of Switzerland's Nestle plans to boost its sales by 30 percent in 1997 to about 20 billion forints ($107.9 million), the Hungarian news agency MTI says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

HONG KONG - Almost anything to do with the year 1997 is marketable in Hong Kong as the British colony makes the transition to Chinese rule. Special edition newspapers will sell at book prices and unique car licence-plates exceed the value of
even luxury cars.

LONDON - Skip that pre-dinner drink if you want to lose weight, Dutch researchers advise, because an aperitif does stimulate the appetite. People who have an alcoholic drink before sitting down to lunch or dinner eat more than those who have fruit juice or water, say researchers at Maastricht
University.

ROME - Italy's best-selling weekly magazine warns readers that Ronaldo, a popular Brazilian soccer player with a huge number of fans, is a symbol of the spendthrift world of professional soccer and Italy's reluctance to confront its problems. The Roman Catholic magazine, Famiglia Cristiana, devotes its cover to what it describes as "Ronalditis" -- which
it calls an "infantile disease of footballing neoliberalism".
HONG KONG - Gurkhas once willing to fight and die defending Britain's empire now acting as guards outside the doors of Hong Kong's imposing banks and swish boutiques.
